oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer token can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by Dex OAuth2/OIDC token usage docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same bearer access token as replay unless the artifact is documented as single-use.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf, or lack of nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5; no Dex doc here requires nbf enforcement
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing nbf checks as a vulnerability by default.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex rotates refresh tokens by default and returns a new refresh token on each refresh.
oidc_jwt.note: A previously used refresh token failing after rotation is expected behavior, not necessarily replay detection on access tokens.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex may accept reuse of the previous refresh token within a configured reuseInterval.
oidc_jwt.note: Short-window refresh token reuse can be by design to tolerate network lag and concurrent requests.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization code flow requests without nonce may succeed.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful code flow without nonce as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex issues bearer-style OAuth2/OIDC tokens that may be reused until expiry unless a specific one-time mechanism is documented.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of a valid unexpired bearer token as replay by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not support refresh tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token for SAML-backed logins is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: After signing key rotation, old keys may remain accepted until JWKS cache or retained-key lifetime expires.
oidc_jwt.source: Dex tokens/signing docs and standard JWKS caching behavior
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag old-key acceptance after the relevant cache/retention window has expired.

oidc_jwt.description: If an admin changes issuer, issuerAlias, discovery overrides, or signing configuration, acceptance under the new trust anchor is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC connector configuration and token signing configuration docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat admin-initiated trust-anchor changes as attacker trust-anchor substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: The SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not support refresh tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token issuance for SAML-backed logins.

oidc_jwt.description: For the upstream OIDC connector, groups claims only refresh when the ID token is refreshed; regular refresh flow does not update groups.
oidc_jwt.note: Stale groups across ordinary refresh should not be flagged as a freshness or authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC connector group claims only refresh when the upstream ID token is refreshed; regular refresh flow does not update groups.
oidc_jwt.note: Stale groups across ordinary refreshes are documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Dex only includes groups when the groups scope is requested and supported by the connector.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing groups claim without the groups scope is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Unsigned or unsupported OIDC request objects may be rejected rather than processed.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection/unsupported outcome is acceptable; only acceptance with altered semantics is security-relevant.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Dex documentation in this corpus exposes no documented REST admin endpoints for enable_auth_method, configure_jwt_validation, create_auth_role, create_policy, create_application, update_application, revoke_session, verify_granted_identity, introspect_token, or cleanup_auth_method. Dynamic management is documented as gRPC-only. The fuzzer MUST NOT invent REST setup or inspection calls for these operations from general Dex knowledge; only the documented OIDC endpoints /auth and /token are available here.

For login_with_password, the fuzzer MUST configure Dex with oauth2.passwordConnector set and include "password" in oauth2.grantTypes. Without passwordConnector, the password grant will not work by design.

For token_exchange, the fuzzer MUST enable grantTypes to include urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, although this grant is enabled by default if grantTypes is omitted. If grantTypes is explicitly set and omits token-exchange, /token exchange tests will fail due to configuration, not security enforcement.

Dex token exchange currently works only with the OIDC connector. The fuzzer MUST configure an upstream OIDC connector and MUST send connector_id in the token exchange request. Omitting connector_id or using a non-OIDC connector makes the test invalid.

For token exchange from upstream access tokens, the upstream OIDC connector MUST have getUserInfo=true if the fuzzer expects Dex to validate opaque access tokens via UserInfo. Without getUserInfo, access-token exchange may fail because Dex cannot validate or enrich the upstream token.

Dex binds issued tokens to OAuth clients. For token_exchange, the client id/secret pair MUST be supplied via HTTP Basic Authentication to /token, even when the client is marked public for this flow. Do not omit client authentication when testing token exchange.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, the fuzzer MUST include scope=openid in start_oidc_auth. Dex documents openid as required for all login requests; missing openid causes setup failure rather than a meaningful security result.

For I3 state-binding tests on the authorization code flow, the fuzzer MUST treat state as session-bound and verify the callback returns the same state sent in start_oidc_auth. Dex documentation explicitly describes state as the mechanism linking the user who started the flow to the one who finished it and preventing replay.

For I2 freshness tests against authorization codes, use Dex expiry.authRequests as the code lifetime control. The fuzzer MUST keep code exchange within that configured window for control logins, and exceed it only for expiry attacks. Otherwise code rejection may be due to normal authRequests expiry.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Dex documents duration fields in config as explicit durations (number + unit such as 10m, 6h) but this corpus does not document any special sentinel where 0 or -1 disables or changes semantics for OIDC token validation. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 means disabled or default for expiry/authRequests/refresh token settings unless separately documented in the concrete deployment config.

For I2 expired_token tests on Dex-issued tokens, the fuzzer MUST use a control login with a valid token alongside the attack login. Dex enforces token expiration on consumed ID tokens and authorization codes, so a failed attack login without a successful control cannot distinguish expiry enforcement from broken client credentials or connector setup.

For I2 future_token and nbf tests against upstream OIDC token exchange, the fuzzer MUST include a control exchange using a valid upstream token from the same connector and client. Without a control, rejection may reflect upstream issuer/client mismatch or connector misconfiguration rather than time-claim enforcement.

For I1/I5 cross-client audience tests, Dex supports cross-client trust via the dynamic scope audience:server:client_id:(client-id), but only when the target client explicitly lists the requesting client in trustedPeers. The fuzzer MUST configure trustedPeers for positive cross-client cases and MUST NOT treat rejection without trustedPeers as an audience-validation bug.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST request only documented Dex scopes (openid, email, profile, groups, federated:id, offline_access, audience:server:client_id:...). Claims outside requested scopes may be absent by design. Compare exchanged-token claims against the requested scope set and connector capabilities, not against an unconstrained superset.

For I5 federated claim tests in token exchange, the fuzzer MUST request scope federated:id if it expects federated_claims in the resulting token. Absence of federated_claims without that scope is by design.

For I5 group-claim tests, the fuzzer MUST request scope=groups and also account for connector-specific group support. Dex documents that some connectors do not support groups, and OIDC connector groups may be disabled unless insecureEnableGroups=true. Missing groups in those cases is not an authorization-binding failure.

For upstream OIDC connector tests targeting I5 group freshness, Dex documents that groups claims only refresh when the ID token is refreshed; the regular refresh flow does not update groups claims. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret stale groups across ordinary refreshes as a security bug unless the test specifically refreshes the upstream ID token path.

For I1 issuer-validation tests when Dex acts as RP to an upstream OIDC provider, the configured connector issuer MUST exactly match the issuer returned by the provider discovery document, unless issuerAlias is intentionally used for off-spec providers. A mismatch here causes expected validation failure and is not evidence of stronger issuer enforcement bypass.

For I1 trust-anchor substitution tests against upstream OIDC, providerDiscoveryOverrides.tokenURL and authURL can intentionally override discovered endpoints, and issuerAlias can override discovered issuer handling for off-spec providers. The fuzzer MUST distinguish admin-authorized overrides from attacker-controlled substitution; success after an admin-configured override is by design.

For I1 alg_none and unsigned request object tests, Dex certification results indicate unsigned request objects may be either supported correctly or rejected as unsupported. The fuzzer MUST treat non-200 rejection as acceptable hardening behavior and MUST NOT require request-object support to consider the platform secure.

For OIDC code-flow nonce tests, Dex certification results show code flow without nonce succeeds. The fuzzer MUST NOT require nonce on pure authorization-code requests to Dex as OP. Missing nonce in code flow is not automatically a vulnerability in this documentation set.

For I3 config-change sequences involving grantTypes, responseTypes, passwordConnector, trustedPeers, issuerAlias, or providerDiscoveryOverrides, a valid test must show the same logical request evaluated inconsistently without an authorized config change. If an admin changes these settings and new logins behave differently, that is by design.

Dex refresh token rotation is enabled by default: every refresh of an ID token issues a new refresh token. The fuzzer MUST capture and use the newest refresh_token after each successful refresh. Reusing an older refresh token outside any configured reuseInterval may fail by design and should not be misclassified as replay protection on bearer access tokens.

Refresh-token testing must account for refreshTokens.disableRotation and refreshTokens.reuseInterval. disableRotation weakens rotation semantics but does not disable refresh-token lifetime controls; reuseInterval allows the same previous refresh token to be accepted within a configured interval. The fuzzer MUST read these settings before classifying refresh-token reuse outcomes.

Dex documentation states some connectors do not support offline_access and therefore do not issue refresh tokens. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a bug when using such connectors; for example SAML ignores offline_access.

For I1/I5 audience tests on consumed ID tokens, Dex documentation and Kubernetes integration notes indicate verifiers are expected to validate aud and iss. The fuzzer MUST use distinct client_ids and verify rejection of tokens minted for a different client unless cross-client trust was explicitly configured.

Dex documentation in this corpus exposes OIDC runtime endpoints but not documented REST admin endpoints for create/update/delete of clients, connectors, policies, users, or auth methods. The fuzzer MUST treat Dex setup as file/static-config or gRPC-managed out-of-band; do NOT invent REST operations such as enable_auth_method, configure_jwt_validation, create_application, or revoke_session from general OIDC knowledge.

Password grant login_with_password works only when oauth2.grantTypes includes "password" and oauth2.passwordConnector is set. Without passwordConnector, password grant requests to /token are not a valid test of credential acceptance.

Token exchange works only with the OIDC connector. For access-token subject tokens, connector config getUserInfo=true is required if Dex must validate opaque access tokens via the upstream UserInfo endpoint. Without this, access-token exchange failures may be setup errors rather than security enforcement.

Dex token exchange additionally requires connector_id in the form body and client credentials via HTTP Basic Authentication. A token-exchange request missing connector_id is not exercising the intended upstream-binding logic.

Public clients in Dex may omit explicit redirectURIs only for redirects beginning with http://localhost or the special urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob value. For authorization-code tests using other redirect URIs, the client must be registered with that exact redirect URI.

Dex supports cross-client trust via the scope audience:server:client_id:(client-id), but the target client must explicitly list the requesting client in trustedPeers. Do NOT interpret successful issuance for another audience as a bug unless trustedPeers was absent.

For I3 state-swap and flow-coherence tests, start_oidc_auth MUST include a unique state value bound to the initiating browser session, and the callback exchange must use the code returned for that same state. Dex documentation explicitly describes state as the mechanism linking the user who started the flow to the one who finished it.

For OIDC code-flow tests, include a nonce in start_oidc_auth and verify it in the returned id_token when the test concerns replay/session binding. Dex certification notes show code flow without nonce may still succeed; absence of nonce enforcement in pure code flow is not by itself a vulnerability.

For I1 request-object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), Dex certification status indicates unsigned request objects may be either correctly supported or rejected as unsupported. The fuzzer MUST treat rejection/unsupported as acceptable and only flag acceptance if an unsigned request object is processed and changes authorization semantics.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Dex-issued tokens, include a control login using a valid authorization flow or valid token exchange in the same environment. Otherwise a /token failure may reflect broken client registration, missing connector_id, or unsupported grant configuration rather than time-claim enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and cross-provider audience tests, Dex-issued tokens are client-bound. The fuzzer MUST vary client_id/audience across distinct registered clients and assert the exchanged or consumed token is rejected when the audience does not match the intended client.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request a narrower initial scope first, then exchange with an expanded scope. Dex docs define scopes as controlling which claims appear in tokens; the oracle must compare returned claims against the original authorization intent, not merely whether exchange succeeded.

For I1/I5 upstream OIDC validation tests on Dex as RP, configure the upstream OIDC connector issuer to exactly match the issuer returned by upstream discovery, unless intentionally testing issuerAlias behavior. Dex docs state issuer MUST match discovery issuer; mismatches otherwise cause setup failure, not a security result.

For I1 issuer-validation tests involving off-spec upstream providers, if issuerAlias is configured then the effective accepted issuer is the alias override rather than the discovery issuer. The fuzzer MUST account for this admin-authorized override and not flag acceptance under the configured alias as trust-anchor substitution.

For I5 group-based authorization tests against the upstream OIDC connector, groups claims are disabled by default unless insecureEnableGroups=true. A missing groups claim under default config is expected and must not be interpreted as claim stripping or authorization failure.

For I5 group freshness tests on the upstream OIDC connector, groups only refresh when the ID token is refreshed; the regular refresh flow does not update groups. Do NOT treat stale groups during ordinary refresh as a vulnerability unless the test specifically performs an ID-token refresh path.

For I5 allowedGroups tests on the upstream OIDC connector, authentication succeeds if the user is a member of at least one configured allowed group. The oracle must not require membership in all configured groups.

For I4 identity-binding tests on token exchange through the OIDC connector, userNameKey/userIDKey determine which upstream claim becomes the Dex user identity. If userNameKey is set to sub, compare granted identity against the submitted sub claim rather than email or preferred_username.

For I4 claim-mapping tests on the upstream OIDC connector, claimMapping only maps a non-standard claim to a standard one if the standard claim is not already present in the id_token, unless overrideClaimMapping=true. The fuzzer MUST set overrideClaimMapping=true when testing whether a mapped alternate claim can replace a present standard claim.

For I5 group filtering tests on the upstream OIDC connector, filterGroupClaims uses RE2 regular expressions, not glob syntax. Wildcards like * are regex operators only in valid regex context; do not treat them as shell-style globs.

For I5 claim-modification tests on the upstream OIDC connector, newGroupFromClaims currently supports only string claims; non-string claims are skipped. Numeric/boolean coercion results here should not be interpreted as authorization bypass unless a string-derived group is actually produced.

For I1/I5 audience tests against Dex as an OpenID Provider, Kubernetes and other consumers are documented to validate aud and iss on Dex-issued ID tokens. When testing Dex-issued tokens as bearer credentials, ensure the verifier is configured with the expected client ID; otherwise acceptance/rejection may reflect verifier configuration, not Dex issuance behavior.

Refresh token rotation has a documented sentinel-like toggle: refreshTokens.disableRotation=true disables every-request rotation, while refreshTokens.reuseInterval permits reuse of the previous refresh token only within the configured interval. Never assume reuseInterval or disableRotation disables underlying expiry checks; validIfNotUsedFor and/or absoluteLifetime still govern refresh-token lifetime.

Dex documentation in this corpus exposes no documented REST admin API for enable_auth_method, configure_jwt_validation, create_auth_role, create_policy, create_application, update_application, revoke_session, cleanup_auth_method, introspect_token, or user CRUD. Test setup for oidc_jwt must therefore be performed via static Dex configuration or the separate gRPC API documentation, not by inventing HTTP admin endpoints.

For token_exchange, the OIDC connector MUST be configured as the upstream connector. Dex documentation states token exchange currently works only with the OIDC connector; using other connector types will fail and is not a security finding.

For token_exchange using upstream access tokens, configure the OIDC connector with getUserInfo=true if the upstream token is an access token. Dex treats access tokens as opaque and validates them by calling the upstream UserInfo endpoint; without getUserInfo, access-token exchange tests may fail due to setup, not security enforcement.

For token_exchange, the request MUST include connector_id naming the upstream OIDC connector. Omitting connector_id makes the request invalid for Dex's exchange flow and can produce false negatives unrelated to JWT validation.

For token_exchange, client authentication is required via HTTP Basic Authentication even when the client is marked public for this flow. The fuzzer must send client_id/client_secret as Basic auth credentials; do not assume anonymous token exchange.

For I5 token-exchange scope escalation tests, Dex issues the exchanged token in the access_token field regardless of requested_token_type, with the actual type indicated by issued_token_type. The oracle must inspect issued_token_type and claims accordingly; do not assume a separate id_token field will be returned.

For I5 cross-client audience tests, Dex-issued tokens are client-bound. The fuzzer MUST vary the downstream client used at /auth or /token and verify audience/azp behavior rather than assuming tokens are audience-agnostic.

For I5 cross-client trust tests, requesting scope audience:server:client_id:(client-id) only works when the target client explicitly trusts the acting client via trustedPeers. Without trustedPeers, failure is expected and not a vulnerability.

For I2 freshness tests on authorization codes, Dex expiry.authRequests controls the time window in which a code can be exchanged. The fuzzer must keep code exchange within that configured lifetime for control logins and outside it only for expiry attacks.

For I2 refresh-token tests, Dex rotates refresh tokens on every refresh by default. Reuse of an old refresh token after a successful refresh is expected to fail and is not a replay bug; if disableRotation or reuseInterval is configured, interpret reuse results in light of that configuration.

Numeric sentinel analysis: refreshTokens.disableRotation is a boolean switch, not a numeric sentinel, but refreshTokens.reuseInterval and other expiry durations are duration values with no documented 0/-1 disable sentinel in this corpus. The fuzzer must not assume 0 or -1 disables validation or means literal zero unless the active Dex config explicitly documents that behavior.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Dex as RP in token_exchange, include a control exchange using a valid upstream token from the same connector. Without a control, rejection of the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken connector configuration, missing getUserInfo, wrong connector_id, or bad client auth.

For I3 state-swap and flow-coherence tests on the authorization code flow, the fuzzer MUST bind state to the initiating browser session and verify the same state is returned on callback. Dex documentation explicitly describes state as the mechanism preventing session mix-up and replay.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the token exchange request must use the same redirect_uri semantics as the authorization request. Dex documentation models a standard OAuth2 code flow; mismatched redirect_uri failures are expected protocol behavior, not identity confusion.

For I3 config-change sequences involving grant types, a login using password grant will only work if oauth2.passwordConnector is configured and password is included in grantTypes. A failed password login without those settings is expected setup failure.

For I1/I5 cross-provider JWT audience tests on token_exchange, configure two distinct upstream OIDC connectors with different issuer/client contexts. Dex documentation requires the submitted subject token to be verified against the issuer configured on the selected connector; tests must vary connector_id to probe cross-connector acceptance.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on the upstream OIDC connector, config.issuer MUST match the issuer returned by upstream discovery unless issuerAlias is intentionally used for off-spec providers. Acceptance after setting issuerAlias may be by design; do not flag it as missing issuer validation unless tokens from an unconfigured issuer are accepted.

For I1 audience validation in Dex's RP behavior, the upstream id_token audience must match the clientID configured for that connector per OIDC validation expectations. Cross-tenant or cross-client token injection tests must ensure the compared connectors actually use different clientIDs; otherwise acceptance is inconclusive.

For I2 nonce-related tests in the authorization code flow, Dex certification results note that code flow without nonce succeeds. The fuzzer must not treat absence of nonce in a code-flow authorization request as a vulnerability by itself; nonce is primarily relevant to front-channel token-returning flows.

For I5 scope/claim tests, Dex only includes claims corresponding to requested scopes: openid is required, email/profile/groups/federated:id add their respective claims. Missing claims outside requested scopes are expected and must not be interpreted as authorization stripping or identity confusion.

For I5 group-based tests against upstream OIDC connectors, groups claims are disabled by default unless insecureEnableGroups=true. A missing groups claim without that setting is expected and not evidence of claim filtering bugs.

For I5 group freshness tests on upstream OIDC connectors, Dex documentation states groups claims only refresh when the ID token is refreshed; the regular refresh flow does not update groups. Do not interpret stale groups during ordinary refresh as an authorization-binding vulnerability unless the test specifically exercises ID-token refresh semantics.

For I4 identity mapping tests on token_exchange through an OIDC connector, the effective upstream identity source is configurable: userIDKey defaults to sub and userNameKey defaults to name. The fuzzer must record which claim is configured as the identity source before asserting collisions or mismatches.

For I4 claim-mapping tests, claimMapping on the OIDC connector only maps non-standard claims to standard ones if the standard claim is not already returned in the id_token, unless overrideClaimMapping=true. Tests expecting remapping to override an existing standard claim must explicitly enable overrideClaimMapping.

For I4/I5 group-name tests, claimModifications.filterGroupClaims uses RE2 regex semantics, while modifyGroupNames prefixes/suffixes all groups and newGroupFromClaims only supports string claims. The oracle must compare against the transformed group values actually emitted by Dex, not the raw upstream groups.
